item.title: Colour the World Orange
item.description:
Monday, 2 November 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Orange to support Colour the World Orange

Significant landmarks light up orange on the first monday of November to raise awareness and support those living with a rare Chronic pain condition called Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS). The Purple Bucket Foundation Inc is a non for profit that started in QLD and is now Australian wide. It raises awareness and supports people who live with CRPS. They also work with universities and other organisations across the world with research and offering services that can help manage this non curable condition

This Light Up is organised by: The Purple Bucket Foundation

Venue address: Kangaroo Point Bridge, Scott Street, Kangaroo Point
Venue type: General Council venue, Light up asset

item.title: Lord Mayor's Charitable Trust Christmas Appeal
item.description:
Thursday, 5 November 2026

Reddacliff Place sculptures will be lit Purple to support the Lord Mayor's Charitable Trust Christmas Appeal

The Lord Mayor’s Charitable Trust has been caring for the Brisbane community since the 1950s. Through a range of critical grant rounds, facilitating connections and support to local and grassroots charities, The Trust makes an impact on Brisbane’s biggest community challenges and most vulnerable residents. The Trust exists to support Brisbane’s frontline charities.
Every year, the Lord Mayor’s Charitable Trust Christmas Appeal raises much needed funds to spread some festive cheer to support charities in Brisbane. In 2024, the Christmas Appeal allowed the Trust to present grants to 93 different charities, bringing joy to families desperately in need within our community. Your support, no matter how big or small, you can make a genuine difference this festive season.

This Light Up is organised by: The Lord Mayor's Charitable Trust

Light up asset: Reddacliff Place, Brisbane City
Venue address: Reddacliff Place, 266 George Street, Brisbane City
Venue type: General Council venue, Light up asset

item.title: Diwali Festival of Lights
item.description:
Friday, 6 November 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit White, Orange and Green to celebrate Diwali Festival of Lights

The Federation of Indian Communities of Queensland (FICQ) invites you to Diwali Festival of Lights, King George Square Friday 6 November 2026.
Diwali is a joyous celebration observed across India, symbolizing the triumph of good over evil. Traditionally, people showcase their creativity by fashioning vibrant rangolis with colours or flowers, adorning the streets with lights, lighting diyas, using eco-friendly firecrackers, and sharing gifts, sweets, and savoury treats. This festival serves as a unifying and uplifting experience for communities throughout India.

This Light Up is organised by: The Federation of Indian Communities of Queensland (FICQ)

item.title: Shine a Light on Lung Cancer
item.description:
Saturday, 7 November 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Green to support Shine a Light on Lung Cancer

Shine a Light on Lung Cancer is Lung Foundation Australia's national community campaign held during Lung Cancer Awareness Month in November. Through community walks and activities across Australia, the campaign brings people together to remember loved ones, stand alongside people living with lung cancer and their families, and raise awareness and vital funds. By illuminating Australian landmarks in Shine a Light green, we aim to create a highly visible symbol of hope and community, encourage conversations about lung cancer, challenge the stigma associated with the disease, and show the thousands of Australians impacted by lung cancer each year that they are seen, supported and not alone

This Light Up is organised by: Lung Foundation Australia

item.title: Neuroendocrine Cancer Day
item.description:
Monday, 9 November 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Blue and Teal to support Neuroendocrine Cancer Day

Neuroendocrine Cancer (NET) Day aims to increase public awareness about neuroendocrine cancers, which are diagnosed in one Australian every 90 minutes, with incidence rates on the rise, making this little known, poorly understood disease Australia's 7th most commonly diagnosed cancer.
By lighting up Brisbane landmarks, NECA seeks to draw attention to the challenges faced by NET patients, Due to the vague symptoms mimicking other conditions 50% of patients are misdiagnosed, with 60% diagnosed at stage four (when the disease is no longer curable) This campaign aims to raise awareness to of NETs to encourage and enable early detection, so there is more chance of a cure and ultimately save lives.

This Light Up is organised by: Neuroendocrine Cancer Australia

Tuesday, 17 November 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Purple to support World Prematurity Day

World Prematurity Day raises awareness of the nearly 15 million babies born premature each year worldwide (one every 2 seconds) and the nearly 1 m babies who lose their fight to survive. It also raises awareness of the need to do more to prevent preterm birth. World Prematurity Day is endorsed by the World health Organisation (WHO) and is now celebrated on 15 November and November is Prematurity Awareness month. Landmarks around Australia and the World are lit purple to raise awareness of the plight of these babies and to honour their struggles to survive. It also helps to raise awareness of and fund charities like PIPA.

This Light Up is organised by: PIPA (Preterm Infants Parents Association)

item.description:
Thursday, 19 November 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Purple to support World Pancreatic Cancer Day

World Pancreatic Cancer Day is held on the third Thursday of November each year, which falls on November 19, 2026. The day is part of Pancreatic Cancer Awareness Month and aims to raise public awareness about the disease, its risks and symptoms, and the importance of early detection, as well as to honour patients and survivors and support the research. Every November, we unite with communities across Australia to wear purple, turn landmarks purple, share stories, hold events, and elevate the voices of those impacted. It’s a time to honour lives, raise visibility, and demand greater focus on this devastating disease.
Join us this November to make pancreatic cancer impossible to ignore.

This Light Up is organised by: Pankind

item.description:

Victoria Bridge will be lit Blue and Green to celebrate Say G'Day Day

Started by Inclusee, Say G’day Day is Australia’s local expression of the global event World Hello Day, which has been celebrated in over 180 countries since 1973. This grassroots movement encourages individuals, organisations, and communities to prioritise social connection as a vital part of good health. The idea is simple: greet ten people to show the power of personal communication in building a more connected community, with the campaign celebrateed by several global partners, including the World Health Organisation's Social Connection Collective.

item.description:
Wednesday, 25 November 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Orange to support International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women

International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women
Each year, the Department of Social Services supports the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and the 16 Days of Activism as the lead federal agency on family, domestic and sexual violence policy. The 16 Days of Activism against gender-based violence is an annual global campaign led by the United Nations, which aims to unite people, communities and organisations worldwide to call for an end to violence against women and girls and promote equality, respect and safety for all. It begins each year on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women (IDEVAW) on 25 November and runs until Human Rights Day on 10 December.

This Light Up is organised by: Department of Social Services

item.title: Lord Mayor's Charitable Trust Christmas Appeal
item.description:
Sunday, 29 November 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Purple to support the Lord Mayor's Charitable Trust Christmas Appeal

The Lord Mayor’s Charitable Trust has been caring for the Brisbane community since the 1950s. Through a range of critical grant rounds, facilitating connections and support the to local and grassroots charities, The Trust makes an impact on Brisbane’s biggest community challenges and most vulnerable residents. The Trust exists to support the Brisbane’s frontline charities.
Every year, the Lord Mayor’s Charitable Trust Christmas Appeal raises much needed funds to spread some festive cheer to support the charities in Brisbane. In 2024, the Christmas Appeal allowed the Trust to present grants to 93 different charities, bringing joy to families desperately in need within our community. Your support the, no matter how big or small, you can make a genuine difference this festive season.

This Light Up is organised by: The Lord Mayor's Charitable Trust

Light up asset: Kangaroo Point Bridge, Kangaroo Point
Venue address: Kangaroo Point Bridge, Scott Street, Kangaroo Point
